insight: tiller Session.run/1 is a blocking GenServer.call with the entire recursive loop inside handle_call/3 (session.ex), AND spawn_subagent calls Session.run/1 synchronously (actions.ex). Any async/observability work must change BOTH paths; inverting the session loop alone does not unblock the parent. Codex verified this against source after an initial 30-line estimate that was 3-5x low.

tiller is event-sourced not checkpointed: Tiller.State.log returns [{action,result}] and Tiller.FakeDriver.context takes a list of actions, so a recorded trajectory prefix is already a valid FakeDriver script and state-at-turn-N is Enum.take(log,n). No checkpointer needed. CAVEAT: replaying actions re-executes tools via Actions.eval, so deterministic replay requires injecting the recorded RESULT, not just replaying the action.

In this environment a compression hook lossily rewrites Bash stdout (drops words, collapses prose to telegraphic form). Reading structured content via `cat`/`sed` in Bash corrupts it — gstack skill section templates came back with placeholder blocks replaced by [->LNN] dedup pointers and unreadable prose. Use the Read tool for skill sections, templates, and any doc whose exact wording matters. A subagent reviewing a design doc hit the same class of problem with the Read summarizer and had to verify via sed/cat -A.

seed mcp serve wraps every port envelope as one text content item in the tools/call result; isError mirrors ok=false. Refusals carry error + exit (2 contention, 3 invalid transition, 4 not found, 6 fenced out); an unknown tool is a JSON-RPC -32602 error, not an envelope. task_get returns state at the top level and the card under "card", not under "task" (task is the id).

An open-seed instantiation on the fastcards backend (copy .seed/, set backend = "fastcards", git init + commit, seed init) is enough to drive the real engine with no remote and no credentials. Adding the test actor to [operators].actors lets it promote its own cards so claim paths are reachable.

First divergence between a trajectory and a branch forked from it is a turn-by-turn prefix walk: the fork shares the parent's prefix by construction, so an inserted turn is itself the divergence and no edit distance is needed. The hard part moved to equality: raw == is wrong on real logs (pids, refs, stack traces, timestamps), so divergence needs a normalizing projection with a caller override.

A tool executes inside the session GenServer's handle_info, so any GenServer.call from a tool to its own session deadlocks (hit it in spawn_subagent asking for the parent id). Pass session identity to tools through the process dictionary (Session.current_id/0), not via call. Same trap applies to any future tool that wants to read its own session's state mid-turn: read Tiller.State, not the Session.

Replay fits the existing seam as a third driver reply, {:replay, action, result, ctx}, that the session records without evaluating. No session mode, no flag, and the replay driver composes with any delegate. The fork point is then just 'how many events to hand the replay driver', and every mutation reduces to (delegate, delegate ctx, whitelist, overrides, latency).

phoenix and phoenix_live_view ship UMD bundles in priv/static (globals Phoenix and LiveView). Two Plug.Static plugs pointed at {:phoenix, "priv/static"} and {:phoenix_live_view, "priv/static"} plus a 4-line inline script give a working LiveSocket with no esbuild, npm, or node. LiveView 1.2 tests need lazy_html (precompiled NIF), not floki.

HEEx :for takes exactly one generator with no filters (a filter clause is a syntax error), and module attributes cannot hold anonymous functions. Precompute filtered lists in render/1 and keep preset behavior in function clauses keyed by string.

Phoenix.Endpoint.server?/2 reads the endpoint's :server key with Keyword.get_lazy and only falls back to :phoenix :serve_endpoints (what `mix phx.server` sets) when the key is absent. An explicit `server: false` in config.exs therefore makes `mix phx.server` start the app silently without binding a port: no error, no log line. Leave the key out and set `server: true` only under PHX_SERVER, the way the generators do. Also: origin checking compares against url: [host:], so a browser on 127.0.0.1 gets 403 on the websocket unless check_origin lists both names.

To make a supervisor restart resume rather than duplicate, store the process's packet (config plus lineage) in a store keyed by the id passed in the start args, and have init/1 branch on whether the packet exists. The restart then re-derives state from the store. With an event log this is a fork of the dead session at its death turn, so replay and resume_ctx are reused as-is and the resumed trajectory can be compared to the original for equality.

DynamicSupervisor's default max_restarts: 3 in max_seconds: 5 counts across all children. A lab that kills several branches on purpose within seconds trips it, the supervisor exits, its parent restarts it empty, and every resumed session vanishes with no error in the tests that expected it. Raise the valve where kills are the feature.

When perturbations have no shared scale, rank by their effect on the shared object instead: for trajectory mutations, the first divergence turn (later = smaller change) gives a partial order with no invented weights, with within-axis size as a tiebreaker and cross-axis ties left as ties.
